issues.claim: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110 (cited as 'RFC 9110: HTTP semantics, conditional requests'; used for 'a failed If-Match condition is 412' and 409 for a state conflict)
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt comes from the redirected info page. It shows only the IANA status code table (409 Conflict, 412 Precondition Failed). It does not show that a failed If-Match yields 412 or what 409 means, and the link has no section fragment. I know from the RFC that If-Match failure gives 412 (section 13.1.1 / 15.5.13), but the excerpt cannot confirm it.
issues.suggestedFix: Link the exact sections: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-13.1.1 (If-Match) and #section-15.5.13 (412). Optionally also cite #section-15.5.10 (409). Re-fetch so the excerpt shows the cited text.

issues.claim: `ExecuteUpdate`, `ExecuteDelete` and raw SQL do not check the token by themselves
issues.problem: The claim is correct, but the cited concurrency page does not support it. Step 2 (migration locks while filling a rowversion column) is also uncited. The text hedges step 2 with 'can', which is fine.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a link to the EF Core ExecuteUpdate/ExecuteDelete docs (learn.microsoft.com/en-us/ef/core/saving/execute-insert-update-delete), or keep the wording as is.

issues.claim: `412 Precondition Failed` for If-Match, `409 Conflict` for a body field
issues.problem: The stub's answerHinge says 'an agreed 409 conflict response'. The 412/409 split is more correct per RFC 9110, and the answer also covers 428. It still deviates from the stub, which the generator already flagged for the owner.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the split. Optionally add one sentence that the team may agree on 409 alone if clients cannot handle 412.

issues.claim: Что станет с уже написанным кодом, который загружает сущность, меняет свойство и вызывает `SaveChanges`?
issues.problem: The hint points directly at the central risk (silently lost edits), which is the core of answerHinge. It is a strong nudge, but the answer also covers numbers, decision options and team rules, so it does not give everything away.
issues.suggestedFix: Soften it, e.g. 'Which assumptions does the existing write code make about the entities it loads, and which part of the application relies on them?'

issues.claim: `Update` marks all properties of the entity and its reachable graph as modified; `Attach`/`Update` can fail if an instance with the same key is already tracked
issues.problem: Both statements are correct. They are not on the two cited pages, which cover tracking, no-tracking, identity resolution and the overhead of tracking. They come from the disconnected-entities docs.
issues.suggestedFix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/ef/core/saving/disconnected-entities as a third link with matching linkTitles in ru and en.

issues.claim: Its `SaveChanges` can be overridden to throw
issues.problem: Overriding only the synchronous SaveChanges leaves the async path open, so writing through the context is still possible.
issues.suggestedFix: Say 'override SaveChanges and SaveChangesAsync (the virtual overloads) to throw'.

issues.claim: Projections into DTOs through `Select` (they create no tracked entities)
issues.problem: This holds only when the projection does not include entity instances. A projection that embeds an entity, such as an anonymous type with an entity member, is still tracked.
issues.suggestedFix: Add 'if the projection contains no entity instances'.
